title: Environmental Monitoring and Alarms
summary: Interpret synthetic thermal telemetry, alarms, and sensor uncertainty.
objectives: Compare environmental trends and alarm states.
Explain why alarms require investigation rather than automatic diagnosis.

vocab.def: Recorded measurements or status data from a system.
A scenario-specific point used to flag attention.
Confidence that a reading represents the condition being observed.

sections.heading: Read the trend
sections.body: Use inlet, exhaust, humidity, airflow, fan, cooling-unit, and alarm data together. Scenario-specific operating limits must be labeled with their context.

sections.heading: Check the signal
sections.body: One sensor may be wrong. Compare multiple readings and trends before naming a cause.

practice.prompt: A temperature alarm appears on one sensor while nearby sensors remain stable. What is a safe next step?
practice.answer: Record the discrepancy, compare relevant evidence, and escalate for authorized investigation.

reflectionPrompt: How can multiple readings improve confidence?
